key_insight: GracefulRL trains language models to preserve normal task performance while learning to safely fall back when success looks unreliable, instead of encouraging risky guessing.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for safety-critical software and automation, where a model should avoid producing harmful outputs or actions when confidence is low.
method: Use outcome-level reinforcement learning reward signals rather than fallback annotations.
Reshape optimization to make graceful failure stable under policy gradients.
Learn an explicit safe fallback policy that activates when acting is likely to be unreliable.
evidence_signal: Across a range of tasks and model scales, the abstract reports models that keep most task-solving ability while selectively falling back when success is out of reach.
watch_item: The abstract notes that naive policy-gradient training with intermediate fallback rewards is brittle, so careful optimization design is essential.
paper_title: Training Language Models to Fail Gracefully
